text:
support-alex: Heads up — we're getting a support escalation (case #5821). Customer sees 500s from the hosted API (/v1/generate). Multiple correlated X-Request-IDs in the case, example: 5f2c9b7a-req-11. Anyone oncall?
ops-jin: I'm on. Do we have request IDs + gateway logs? Which cluster/region?
support-alex: Customer in us-west-2. Example curl they sent:
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx' -H 'X-Request-ID: 5f2c9b7a-req-11' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response was a 500 with body "quota service error". Support attached gateway headers showing upstream status 502.
carol-eng: Pinging quota-orch metrics now. Seeing a burst of RPC timeouts to quota-store at ~12:18 UTC, spans >2s. Also a new rollout to rlimit-router-v2 happened ~12:10. Could be related.
maya-sre: Looking at envoy logs: upstream_reset before connect for quota-orch, code 504 / connection timeout. Stack shows gateway routed to quota-orch internal VIP that resolves to rlimit-router-v2 pool.
oncall-bot: Incident Alert: increased 5xx on /v1/generate (us-west-2) — 12:15–12:25 spike, peak p50 latency 1100ms, error rate 6.8% :warning:
ember-support: Customer reports it started after they ramped traffic. They were under quota but got 500s instead of 429. This is bad for integrations.
ops-jin: Quick repro: hitting same endpoint with X-Request-ID above returns 500 consistently for me. Captured gateway trace:
```
[proxy] -> quota-orch (tcp connect timeout)
quota-orch -> auth-cache (rpc deadline exceeded)
quota-orch: uncaught exception -> return 500
```
carol-eng: The rlimit-router-v2 change accidentally removed a per-request timeout bump and also changed route to use cluster "quota-store-v2" which doesn't have healthy hosts in us-west-2 (misconfigured subset). So requests time out and quota-orch raises a 500 instead of mapping to 429.
maya-sre: Mitigation options: 1) rollback rlimit-router-v2 route (fast) 2) add gateway classification to map quota-orch timeout -> 429 for client-visible responses 3) emergency permissive policy for affected customers.
ops-jin: Rolling back the routing change now. I'll also flip a temporary routing rule to prefer quota-store-v1.
carol-eng: Rolled back at 12:22 UTC — observing error rate drop. Current error rate down to 0.6% and falling. Can confirm quota-store-v1 pool healthy.
support-alex: I told the customer we have a rollback and will follow up with a timeline. They accepted.
ana-product: Follow-ups: we need a postmortem. Action items: add a pre-deploy check that validates cluster health for new route subsets, ensure quota-orch maps dependency timeouts -> 429 or 503 (not 500), and add regression test for high-latency quota-store.
maya-sre: Agreed. I will open a postmortem ticket and add observability for rlimit-router rollout diffs. Also we should add a circuit-breaker to quota-orch to fail-fast with client-facing 429 when upstream is degraded.
support-alex: Thanks all. I'll update the case thread and send the rollback timeline + request IDs to the customer. :white_check_mark:
